EN-b33cee.en: / result=2 means this handset still belongs to another register (hoop-pmo) — routine when a phone comes across from Hoop, not a fault. Releasing it in Hoop's portal is not enough: that unlocks the handset and gives up ownership but leaves its token in place, so it still answers this way. The app writes its server address only when it holds no token, so -e server is silently ignored on a phone that has one — which is why the claim 403s: it is asking the wrong office. Do not use -e current; it moves the token and keeps the old server, leaving a phone no register can reach. Release it over the cable with its token from that register (result=1 or result=3 both clear it), then run steps 1 and 2 again. result=3 keeps ownership, so step 1 can be skipped.
EN-b33cee.sw: / result=2 inamaanisha simu hii bado ni ya rejista nyingine (hoop-pmo) — ni jambo la kawaida simu inapotoka Hoop, si hitilafu. Kuiachilia kwenye mfumo wa Hoop haitoshi: hiyo hufungua simu na kuacha umiliki, lakini huacha token yake, kwa hiyo bado hujibu hivi. Programu huandika anwani ya seva yake tu isipokuwa ina token, kwa hiyo -e server hupuuzwa kimya kwenye simu iliyo nayo — ndiyo maana madai yanapata 403: inauliza ofisi isiyo sahihi. Usitumie -e current; huhamisha token na kuacha seva ya zamani, na kuacha simu ambayo hakuna rejista inayoweza kuifikia. Iachilie kwa kebo kwa kutumia token yake kutoka kwenye rejista hiyo (result=1 au result=3 zote huiondoa), kisha endesha hatua ya 1 na ya 2 tena. result=3 huweka umiliki, kwa hiyo hatua ya 1 inaweza kurukwa.
